name: Elzabad
overview: Elzabad was a male member of the tribe of Gad who played a role in the support of David during his time at Ziklag. He is specifically noted as the ninth Gadite to join David, highlighting his part in the gathering of warriors who aligned with David's leadership. His presence at Ziklag marks him as one of the early followers who contributed to David's consolidation of support.
namesAndTitles: The name Elzabad means 'G-d has given,' reflecting a recognition of divine provision. This proper name is recorded in 1 Chronicles 12:12 and does not indicate that it was given directly by God but carries a meaningful theistic affirmation common in Hebrew names.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Elzabad as a descendant of Gad, linking him to one of the twelve tribes of Israel. Beyond this tribal affiliation, no further family relationships are recorded in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Elzabad's significance lies in his role as one of the Gadite warriors who came to David at Ziklag, demonstrating the growing support for David among the tribes of Israel. Being the ninth Gadite to join David emphasizes the organized and deliberate nature of this allegiance. His mention in 1 Chronicles 12:12 situates him within the larger narrative of David's rise to kingship and the unification of Israel under his leadership.
